exposure: geographical origin (Shahdol, Umaria, other districts vs Anuppur)
cohort: The study included pregnant women requiring caesarean section at Medical College, Shahdol, India, from May to July 2023.
finding: The study found a 13.4% SSI rate post-caesarean section, with significant predictors including caesarean section duration < 30 min and subcutaneous skin closure, and higher SSI risk for women referred from Shahdol, Umaria, and other districts compared to Anuppur, attributing high SSI incidence to an erratic referral system.
mod_finding: Caesarean section duration < 30 minutes and subcutaneous skin closure were identified as significant predictors for surgical site infection following caesarean birth.
